note: Civil edits to the measured ground, per location, applied in this order by scripts/twin/build-terrain.mts (P03a). Location frame, metres, Y up; y = 0 is the location's origin elevation.

pad: a level bench. Inside `rect` [xMin, zMin, xMax, zMax] the ground is `level`; outside, it meets the hill with a cut (benched: faces of `faceGrade` rise per run (a face as steep as the hill behind it runs on up the hill, so cuts in this steep ground are steep: 2.5, about 68 degrees, as the site's laterite and rock cuts stand in the owner's photographs), `benchHeight` high, with `berm` metres of flat between) or a fill (`fillGrade`). `face` is the material of cut faces: shotcrete or laterite (bare soil, with rock where steep). Toe drains run along the foot of every cut face over 1 m.
patch: a finished ground asset (P02a); its own heights are used inside it and the hill is cut or filled to meet its edge.
channel: a cut with a level floor and steep sides.

road: a shelf road (cut faces 2.2 rise per run, 6 m benches) along `points` (x, z), its levels found from the ground with grades up to `maxGrade`, pinned where a point gives a third value (y). Concrete where the grade passes `concreteFrom`. `width` is the running surface.

streams: the river and gullies found from the elevation model (catchment of `minAreaKm2` or more), carved as a V with a cobble bed; `pin` sets the bed level at one point (the elevation model reads the forest canopy, so beds read high).
provisional: true marks an edit kept from v1's arrangement that a later phase replaces. skip: a reason; the edit is listed but not applied.

reroutes.source: The model's line (30 m data) runs diagonally through the yard. The storm drain plan (R3) has the floodwall on the river side south and south-west of the powerhouse and the tailraces discharging south to the river: the river is moved round the yard's south side, past the tailrace outlet
The gully from the west ran across the yard's south-west corner; moved outside the pad to join the river below the tailrace

pin.source: Tailrace outlet: the bed must sit below the turbine floor (EL 188.24, drawing R1) and the yard (EL 188.04); the floodwall and tailrace on the storm drain plan (R3) put the river just below the yard

edits.source: Yard level EL 188.04 (penstock plan, MPR-53 slide 65). Machine hall 31.5 m across the penstock axis with a 7.3 m annex and the switchyard on +x (R1, R3). The hill behind is cut in shotcreted benches (MPR-53 photos)
Big and small tailraces join and discharge to the river through a flared outlet with riprap (R3). Floor level is this session's estimate between the lower pit (EL 183.54) and the river bed

edits.skip: On the real ground this corner of v1's pad sits 10 to 60 m below the hill and would need a benched cut 60 m deep; the real main camp is about 400 m away and P06 builds its bench. The gate's own patch is cut into the hill instead
edits.source: v1's Temfacil pad (terrainData.ts, cut to 13.0 m) behind the camp gate. The real main camp is about 400 m from the powerhouse (site-layout.json); P06 replaces this bench

AR01 as traced off the site development plan (site-layout.json, `ar01`, error 10 to 25 m). The last 150 m, traced along the river bed, are moved onto the north-west bank, 25 to 35 m from the river, to reach the yard's south-west corner across the west gully (a ford)

Yard to the camp gate. The traced powerhouse-to-camp line (site-layout.json) leaves the yard's north-east corner, but the gate is 12.7 m up: the ramp is wound out along the hill to keep it near 19 percent, concreted (as v1's ramp was)

Gate to the main camp and on towards the weir: the traced line (site-layout.json `powerhouse-to-main-camp`, then `ar02`), joined to the gate slice's own road where it leaves the patch. The trace runs 0 to 16 m off the stream's line, in its bed in places: held on the north bank, about 20 m from the stream, crossing it by a ford where it turns north for the weir
The P02a slice's ground (approved 2026-10-15), kept exactly; v1's ground under it was the camp pad's corner
